title: Impact-weighted pager reduction and automated multi-region cutover runbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Our current paging flood during transient SLO deviations leads to frequent on-call fatigue and slower remediation of genuinely high-impact incidents. We need a pragmatic system that reduces noise while preserving rapid response for customer-visible failures. Goal: implement an impact-weighted paging layer plus an automated cutover runbook that (1) predicts short-term SLO drift using percentile-slope heuristics, (2) mutes low-impact transient alerts automatically with exponential backoff and synthetic canary gating, and (3) ties circuit-breaker-driven load-shedding to an automated multi-region cutover sequence when capacity breach is predicted. Constraints: cannot alter existing SLI definitions, must integrate with PagerDuty and Opsgenie, rollout must be reversible and observable, and any automated cutover requires human confirmation at defined checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume for low-impact SLO breaches drops by >=60% in the staged canary region during peak synthetic test
High-impact incidents (customer-visible errors) still produce immediate P1 pages with full context and escalation intact
Automated cutover workflow can execute a controlled traffic shift to a secondary region with <5% additional latency and documented rollback path
Dashboards expose pre-cutover predictor confidence, suppression decisions, and the last 7 days of automatic mutes for audit
Runbook is reviewed and approved by oncall leads and SRE manager (signoff linked)
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Predictor prototype: build a rolling 5m and 30m percentile slope detector for token-error rate and tail-latency; tune thresholds per route tier

Phase 2 - Suppression layer: implement a middleware that evaluates impact-score (request rate * error-severity * customer-tier) and applies staged mute rules with exponential backoff and synthetic-canary gating
Phase 3 - Circuit-breaker integration: expose predictor hooks to the runtime CB service to allow progressive shedding and prepare cutover if predicted capacity breach persists >2 minutes

Phase 4 - Runbook automation: author an automated cutover pipeline (scripts + orchestration) that performs staged DNS steering, load balancer priority change, and regional cache warmup with human checkpoints and automatic rollback on health regressions
Phase 5 - Observability & audit: create dashboards and logs, surface all auto-mute decisions in the console, and add an approvals/audit trail for any automated region cutover
Phase 6 - Canary rollout: test in a synthetic canary pool, then 1% of production traffic for 48h before full rollout
runbook_excerpt: Trigger criteria: predictor confidence >0.85 for 3 consecutive 1m windows OR circuit-breaker enters HYSTERESIS state with sustained >90th percentile tail-latency

Step 1 - Alert triage: on-call receives an annotated page with impact_score and predictor chart; follow checklist: confirm scope (region/routes/customers) and validate against synthetic canary dashboard
Step 2 - Suppression check: if impact_score < threshold_low, acknowledge and allow auto-mute to complete; add note and analysis_gist link
Step 3 - Prepare cutover: if impact_score >= threshold_high and predictor persists >2m, run "prepare_cutover" script which pre-warms caches in target region and pauses non-essential jobs

Step 4 - Human checkpoint: send a confirmation DM to SRE lead with a 3-minute countdown; if approved, execute staged traffic shift (10% -> 50% -> 100%), monitoring latency and error SLI after each step
Step 5 - Rollback: if any step causes error-rate to increase >20% or latency >SLO by >50% after 2m, immediately rollback to previous region and open post-mortem ticket
Post-incident: attach predictor logs, suppression decisions, and timeline to the incident ticket and mark auto-mute decisions for quarterly audit
metrics_and_queries: SLO drift predictor query: SELECT pctile(95, latency) OVER (sliding_window 5m) - pctile(95, latency) OVER (sliding_window 30m) AS p95_slope
Impact score: impact = requests_per_min * error_weight * customer_tier_multiplier
Suppression audit: count(auto_mute=true) by route, reason, duration in last 7d
Cutover health check: sum(successful_requests)/sum(total_requests) by region over 1m windows

notes: Trade-offs discussed: Conservative suppression reduces noise but risks hiding early signals; mitigated by predictor confidence and synthetic canaries
We decided against autonomous rollback without human sign-off for the initial two releases due to blast-radius concerns
This work complements but does not replace existing SLO alert thresholds; it's an overlay that annotates and suppresses noisy pages where safe
